issue.title: Mid-stream upstream failure (Z.ai 502 / connection reset) leaves Pi with malformed SSE and hangs, even though failover works before the first byte
issue.body:
## Summary

When the upstream provider (Z.ai, glm-5.3) fails in the middle of a streamed reply, Pi prints `Error: Error reading response: malformed server-sent event JSON.` and then hangs. It never recovers, and I have to interrupt it manually.

Failover works when an account fails before any output is sent, but once a reply has started, the failure reaches Pi as a broken stream.

## Setup

- Agent: Pi
- Model: `glm-5.3` via the Z.ai provider, reasoning level `low`
- Routing: a group with three Z.ai accounts (one was already resting because of a 429 insufficient-balance error)
- Context size when it happened: about 78k / 1.0M

## What happened

1. Pi sends a request for `glm-5.3` through the magpie gateway.
2. Account `e68d…utRM` returns 502 before any output. magpie rests it for 1 minute and forwards the request to `5f32…pQvJ`. This part works as intended.
3. Account `5f32…pQvJ` starts answering, then the upstream connection breaks.
4. Pi shows `Error: Error reading response: malformed server-sent event JSON.` and hangs. It does not retry and does not return to the prompt.

## Gateway log (Routing view)

```
42d8…49iZ is resting (429 · insufficient balance, back in 19 min), placed last.
e68d…utRM (glm-5.3) at low reasoning returned 502 · failed. It rests 1 min, longer if it fails again; the request was forwarded to 5f32…pQvJ before the reply reached Pi.
Original: Post "https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4/chat/completions": read tcp [REDACTED]:51313->[REDACTED]:443: read: connection reset by peer
5f32…pQvJ (glm-5.3) at low reasoning broke after starting to answer · failed. Pi received the content already output before the error; it rests 1 min, longer if it fails again; Pi's next request goes to the other members first.
```

## Upstream response

The upstream payload from Z.ai for the failed request:

```json
{
  "id": "202610220001118dfb145dcf634908",
  "model": "glm-5.3",
  "choices": [
    {
      "type": "message",
      "reasoning": "Attempt3 got past CF (422) but wrong ToS field name. Try common names: \"tos_accepted\", \"agreed_to_terms\", \"accept_terms\", \"terms\": true, \"acceptTos\". One more round quickly"
    }
  ],
  "error": {
    "message": "Z.ai: connection lost mid-reply (http2: client connection lost)",
    "type": "api_error"
  }
}
```

The `reasoning` text is part of the partial reply and is unrelated to this bug. Note that this error object is not a standard Chat Completions error: it has `choices[].reasoning` and a top-level `error` in the same body.

## Analysis

- The upstream failure itself (Z.ai returning 502 / resetting the connection) is outside magpie's control.
- Failover works when the upstream fails **before** any output (the e68d → 5f32 hop).
- When the upstream fails **after** output has started, magpie cannot switch accounts, so it forwards the partial output to Pi. Pi then receives an SSE event it cannot parse (either a truncated event, or the upstream error object forwarded in a shape Pi does not accept) and hangs.
- So the problem looks like how the stream is terminated after a mid-stream failure, not the failover logic.

## Expected behavior

After forwarding partial output, magpie should end the stream with a well-formed error event that the agent's protocol parser accepts, then close the connection. For example, with Chat Completions: a valid error chunk followed by `data: [DONE]`. Pi should then be able to show the error or retry and return to the prompt, instead of hanging.

## Actual behavior

Pi reports `malformed server-sent event JSON` and hangs until interrupted manually.

## Suggestions

- Normalize mid-stream upstream errors (including the non-standard Z.ai error body above) into a valid error event for the protocol the agent is using, and always close the stream afterwards.
- If the upstream connection drops after partial output, make sure the gateway never writes a truncated SSE event to the agent.

comments.body:
The relay already ended a stream whose upstream died mid-reply with the protocol's own error event, but what it appended began after a blank line — and that blank line completed whatever half line the upstream's last write had left standing into an event of its own. Pi read that event's truncated JSON as `malformed server-sent event JSON` and hung, the error event after it unread; a Chat stream ended with no `[DONE]` either. Failover before the first byte was never the problem (the report's own e68d… → 5f32… hop shows it working), and once output has started the gateway cannot switch accounts, so the fix is in how the relayed stream ends.

**What changed** (internal/gateway/gateway.go, the passthrough relay):

- A stream's last line — the one a read left unfinished — is no longer the client's until it ends: held back, handed on when the stream ends cleanly, dropped when the read fails. A severed upstream can no longer leave a half event behind. A body that is not events (a plain JSON reply) goes through as it came, and a held line that outgrows any event (1 MiB, the same bound where the usage sniffer gives up on a runaway line) is handed on unheld, so nothing buffers without end.
- A stream the read failed on now ends, after its error event, with `data: [DONE]` when the client speaks Chat Completions — the end the report asks for, so a client reading to `[DONE]` stops there and says the error it read. A stream that ended cleanly but short still ends at the error event: there a `[DONE]` would read the cut reply as whole, which TestGeminiCompatRelayEndedShort pins. Anthropic (`event: error`), Responses (`response.failed`) and Gemini end on their error events as they did; Gemini's stream has no `[DONE]`.
- Whether a mid-stream failure joins the group's own failover stays as it is: the agent retries its own stream, which is the ending #3197 asks for, and nobody rests or re-asks here.

**Red before the fix** — two tests in internal/gateway/passthrough_severed_test.go, a fake upstream that serves valid chunks and then dies inside a data line under a lying Content-Length (no network). On base `9b0f4861` with the tests alone:

```
--- FAIL: TestPassthroughChatSeveredMidLine (0.10s)
    passthrough_severed_test.go:137: the severed stream left an event no client can read: "{\"id\":\"c1\",\"model\":\"m\",\"cho"
--- FAIL: TestPassthroughChatSeveredAtLineEnd (0.01s)
    passthrough_severed_test.go:172: the error event was not followed by [DONE]: connection lost mid-reply (unexpected EOF)","type":"api_error"}}
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gateway	1.032s
```

With the fix both pass: every event the client can read parses as JSON (or is `[DONE]`), the error stands, and `[DONE]` follows it. Ablation: the product back to base with the tests kept, both fail again; restored, green. A first shape of this fix appended `[DONE]` after every failure event; the full gateway suite turned up TestGeminiCompatRelayEndedShort, which pins a cleanly-cut reply as ending exactly at the error event — the `[DONE]` now belongs to the severed case only, and the suite is green at the submitted head.

**Siblings** — the protocols' mid-stream exits, one by one:

- Chat passthrough (this fix): the half event is kept from the client, and the severed case ends `[DONE]`.
- Chat translated (streamTranslated): the error event is synthesized from events magpie decoded, so no half line can reach the client, and the stream ends on the connection's close after the error. Its missing `[DONE]` is the same shape but has no report and no failing case, so it stands as it is.
- Anthropic passthrough: `event: error` is terminal for its clients; a `message_stop` after an error would say the reply completed. Unchanged.
- Responses passthrough: `response.failed` likewise terminal. Unchanged.
- Gemini passthrough: ends on a candidate's finishReason, and its OpenAI-compatible relay has no `[DONE]` to add; TestGeminiCompatRelayEndedShort is green at this head. Unchanged.
- In flight: my #2873 patch (hunt48-e-cutshort-retry) classifies a plugin's cut-short error and re-asks the same member — routing policy, not the wire; it sits in serve's try loop and routing.go's failure words, not in the relay's write path. The two compose: this patch decides what the client's stream ends with, that one whether the gateway asks again.

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Red on base | `go test -run '^(TestPassthroughChatSeveredMidLine\|TestPassthroughChatSeveredAtLineEnd)$' ./internal/gateway/`, gateway.go at `9b0f4861`, tests kept | FAIL ×2, excerpt above |
| Green with the fix | the same, fix restored | ok |
| Ablation round trip | product to base and back | FAIL ×2 → ok |
| Severed and Gemini-compat families | `go test -run 'Passthrough\|Severed\|LoopCut\|StreamCut\|NonStream\|GeminiCompat\|Gemini' ./internal/gateway/` | ok |
| Race | `go test -race -run 'Passthrough\|Severed\|LoopCut\|GeminiCompat' ./internal/gateway/` | ok |
| Full changed package | `go test -tags nogui -count=1 ./internal/gateway/` | ok, 318s |
| Format | `gofmt -l` on the two changed files | empty |
| Vet | `go vet ./...` darwin; `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...`; `GOOS=windows go vet -tags nogui ./...` | clean (darwin prints a pre-existing cgo warning in internal/gui/trayimage_darwin.go, a file this patch never touches) |
| Builds | `go build`; `GOOS=linux go build -tags nogui`; `GOOS=windows go build` | ok |
| Patch applies | `git am` of the patch below on a fresh `9b0f4861` worktree | applies; the gateway package is then identical to the branch's |

**What the client reads now**: only whole lines, then the protocol's error event — for Chat one it can parse and show, then `[DONE]` — and a close. An upstream failure and a normal end tell apart again: a normal end is the reply's own last event (or `[DONE]`), a failed one carries the error naming the provider.

**Not verified**: against a real Z.ai account — the fake delivers the shape the report describes (a 200 stream that stops mid-line, connection reset) but no real account was spent on it; Pi's own reader is not run here — that the hang ends once the stream is well-formed rests on #470 and #1644's accounts of pi-ai, not on a Pi run; the suite ran on darwin only (Linux and Windows are vet and build, not test); the 1 MiB runaway-line hand-on rests on the sniffer's same bound rather than a test of its own.

Branch with the commit: [hunt59-d-3197-midstream-fail](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/hunt59-d-3197-midstream-fail) (head `52f5fbaaa2d88c368b7b082cb6a5fd684a354402`).

**Attribution**: AI-written; I've read the whole diff and the tests pass. Please keep the author (`ggbdpq`) or add `Co-authored-by: ggbdpq <ggbdpq@gmail.com>`.

Implemented on my fork: [a6a2c260](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/a6a2c260e8a2425a8ea5276e46ac6753af9fd9c8), based on ggbdpq's proposed fix, with attribution retained.

The Chat SSE passthrough now retains an incomplete line until it is complete. If the upstream disconnects, the truncated tail is discarded and the gateway sends a separate error event followed by `[DONE]`. Clean EOF still forwards the remaining bytes unchanged.

Both regression tests fail before the change and pass afterward: disconnect mid-line and disconnect at a line boundary. Related passthrough/stream-cut/Gemini compatibility tests passed under the race detector, three runs.

I also replayed the actual before/after gateway output through `@earendil-works/pi-ai@1.1.0`'s OpenAI Completions parser, using only a local fixture. Before: `malformed server-sent event JSON`; after: `UP: connection lost mid-reply (unexpected EOF)`. Both runs retained the received text and emitted a terminal error. This verifies the parser boundary, not the originally reported Pi UI hang.

The buffer is bounded at 1 MiB: a single unterminated line beyond that limit is forwarded and cannot subsequently be repaired on disconnect. No live vendor account was used.

Combined branch: [fix/issue-batch-20261023-g](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/issue-batch-20261023-g), tested at `4b137b7073fe9fac3edea323ca221f7b26d5653f`. Go 1.26.8: native/Linux nogui/Windows vet and builds all passed, plus the full `go test -tags nogui ./... -count=1 -timeout=45m` suite in a temporary HOME. No upstream PR opened.

Verified the adaptation: [a6a2c260](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/a6a2c260e8a2425a8ea5276e46ac6753af9fd9c8) carries the fix from my [comment above](#issuecomment-6325966863) (52f5fba). Re-ran the cycle myself, the commit cherry-picked onto `main` @ 63be4771 (plus the two other hunt66 commits I was verifying beneath it) as 6f2d7eb5, Windows, go 1.26.5.

**Fidelity** — the regression is mine word for word: the 81 lines the commit adds to `passthrough_severed_test.go` (the `severedChat`/`chatEventsSevered` helpers and `TestPassthroughChatSeveredMidLine`/`TestPassthroughChatSeveredAtLineEnd`) diff empty against what my patch adds. The product change in `gateway.go` is the same mechanism reshaped, same semantics: an SSE relay holds the line a read left unfinished, forwards it on a clean end (`rerr == nil || rerr == io.EOF`, my exact condition), drops it on a read failure, bounds the hold at the sniffer's 1 MiB with the overage passed through unheld, and ends a severed Chat stream with `data: [DONE]\n\n` after the error event under my exact guard (`proto == provider.Chat && rerr != nil && rerr != io.EOF` — so a cleanly-cut reply still ends at the error event, `TestGeminiCompatRelayEndedShort` staying the pin). The shape differs: theirs wraps the original write as `rawWrite` and appends-then-splits at the last newline, mine splits-then-appends and keeps the `atLine` bookkeeping inline — two spellings of one behavior, and the ordering the bug is about holds in theirs the same way: the fragment is discarded before `apart()` lays the blank line and the error event down, so nothing can complete the half line into an event, and `[DONE]` follows the error only where the upstream actually severed. Their commit adds one thing mine didn't have: a 10-line paragraph in `docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md`.

The relay already ended a stream whose upstream died mid-reply with the protocol's own error event, but what it appended began after a blank line — and that blank line completed whatever half line the upstream's last write had left standing into an event of its own. Pi read that event's truncated JSON as `malformed server-sent event JSON` and hung, the error event after it unread; a Chat stream ended with no `[DONE]` either. Failover before the first byte was never the problem (the report's own e68d… → 5f32… hop shows it working), and once output has started the gateway cannot switch accounts, so the fix is in how the relayed stream ends.

**What changed** (internal/gateway/gateway.go, the passthrough relay):

- A stream's last line — the one a read left unfinished — is no longer the client's until it ends: held back, handed on when the stream ends cleanly, dropped when the read fails. A severed upstream can no longer leave a half event behind. A body that is not events (a plain JSON reply) goes through as it came, and a held line that outgrows any event (1 MiB, the same bound where the usage sniffer gives up on a runaway line) is handed on unheld, so nothing buffers without end.

issue.body:
## Summary

While investigating `Error reading response: malformed server-sent event JSON.` from an agent talking to the gateway over `/v1/responses`, I captured several streams where **a single SSE frame was internally corrupted**: a contiguous slice of characters was dropped from inside the JSON payload, while the frame still ended with a well-formed tail and every other frame in the same response was valid.

This looks different from the already-reported mid-stream upstream failures (#2580, #3197), where the **stream is cut short** by an upstream reset. Here the HTTP response completed normally (200, `response.completed` received) and only one frame's **content** was damaged.

I want to be upfront: **I could not reproduce this reliably.** It reproduced several times in a short window and then stopped completely. Details and honest caveats are below, because I think the failure mode is worth a look regardless.

## Environment

- magpie version: `0.1.1318` (reported by `GET /`; gateway UI build and PID unchanged across the whole investigation, so no restart/upgrade happened between successes and failures)
- OS: Windows
- Endpoint: `/v1/responses` (OpenAI Responses API), streaming
- Client: an agent using the official `openai` SDK's SSE iterator (`for await (const sse of stream)`, `JSON.parse(sse.data)`)
- Model: DeepSeek-family chat model served via a Responses-compatible provider (identifiers omitted)

## What the client sees

The OpenAI SDK's Responses SSE loop does:

```js
for await (const sse of messages) {
  if (sse.data === '[DONE]') break;
  data = JSON.parse(sse.data);           // no per-frame recovery
}
// on throw:
// SyntaxError: Error reading response: malformed server-sent event JSON.
```

Because there is no tolerance for a single bad frame, one corrupted `data:` line kills the whole turn even though 4000+ other frames in the same response were fine.

## Observed corruption

The damaged frame was always `event: response.created` — the first frame, which **echoes the entire request** back, including `instructions` and the full `tools` array. In my repro that frame was ~64 KB.

Sanitized example (tool descriptions are my own synthetic filler text, repeated to inflate the payload):

```
BAD FRAME #1  (event: response.created)
  frame length : 65885 chars
  parse error  : After parsing a value an unexpected character was encountered: :. Path 'response.tools[2]', line 1, position 16366

  tools present in the echoed array: tool_0, tool_1, tool_5, tool_6, ... tool_29
  tools MISSING                    : tool_2, tool_3, tool_4

  tool_1 description: expected 1680 chars, got 1629 chars  (51 chars dropped)

  corruption join point (verbatim):
    ... number 1. This is a long tool description ray"},"arg1":{"description":"arg one","type":"string"}}},"strict":null},{"type":"function","name":"tool_5","description":"...
```

In another capture the same frame lost a larger block: `tool_1`'s description was short by 51 chars and `tool_2` through `tool_4` vanished entirely, while `tool_5` onward were intact.

Key properties of the corruption:

1. The dropped region is **interior** — the frame ends correctly with `...,"metadata":{}},"sequence_number":0}`.
2. It is **not** a truncation: bytes after the gap are present, `tool_5`'s object is complete.
3. It is **not** an encoding problem: the captured frame round-trips through strict UTF-8 decode/re-encode unchanged, and there are no lone surrogates or replacement characters.
4. It is **isolated** to one frame — the other ~4000 frames of that same response parse fine, and the response ends with `response.completed`.
5. The frame is large (~64 KB), consistent with the echoed request.

## Reproduction attempt

A minimal client that POSTs to `/v1/responses` with `stream: true`, a large `instructions` string, and 30 tools with long descriptions, then strictly validates every `data:` line with a JSON parser.

| Window | Requests | Requests with a corrupted frame |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ~10:58–11:05 | 5 | **3** (60%) |
| ~11:20–11:35 | 40 | **0** |

Between the two windows I changed nothing on the client side and the gateway process (same PID, same version) was never restarted. I replayed the exact same script byte-for-byte in the second window and it passed every time. The captured bad frames from the first window are still on disk and still fail to parse, so this was real damaged output, not a client-side parsing bug.

So: **transient but reproducible-once-present.** I don't have a reliable trigger, which is the main caveat of this report.

## Why I think it's worth reporting despite that

- A single bad frame is unrecoverable for strict SSE clients, and the symptom (`malformed server-sent event JSON`) is identical to #2580/#3197, so it's easy to misattribute to "upstream connection reset" when the upstream here returned a normal, complete 200.
- The trigger seems tied to **large echoed frames**. If the gateway builds `response.created` by serializing the parsed request, any streaming/buffering path that copies chunks rather than whole frames could split multi-byte sequences or drop a chunk under load. A 64 KB frame is the consistent factor across every occurrence.
- Even if the root cause is upstream (a proxy returning a slightly mangled but complete body), the gateway is the only place that can validate frame integrity before forwarding.

## Suggestions

- Validate each outgoing SSE frame is valid JSON before writing it (cheap at the boundary, and converts a silent corruption into a detectable error).
- Specifically for `response.created`: consider whether the echoed request needs to be sent in full. It's the largest non-delta frame in the stream and carries the most redundancy.
- If a frame is found malformed mid-stream, emit a proper error event plus stream termination rather than a corrupt `data:` line, so clients fail cleanly instead of with an opaque parse error.

## Related issues

- #2580 and #3197 both concern malformed SSE, but in both the stream is **terminated early** by an upstream reset. Here the stream completes; only one frame's content is damaged. Possibly the same weak spot at a different layer.
- #1933 (closed) and #1786 (closed) touch Responses streaming and tool-use frames.

## Caveats

- Model/provider identifiers and the upstream hostname are redacted.
- The tool descriptions are synthetic filler text I generated, not real tooling.
- I can't give a reliable repro trigger. If useful, I can share the exact request builder and the raw captured frame (with the filler content) — happy to attach or paste if that helps.

issue.title: Z.ai mid-reply failures (502 / connection reset) reach the agent as malformed or silently truncated streams: error object embedded in a 200 body is not treated as a failure

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

When Z.ai (`glm-5.3`) fails in the middle of a streamed reply, the failure is not handled as an upstream error by the gateway. Two different symptoms have been observed with the same root cause:

1. Pi prints `Error: Error reading response: malformed server-sent event JSON.` and then hangs until interrupted.
2. The response body contains the partial reply plus a top-level `error` object, even though it does not look like an error response (see "Second occurrence"). A gateway that only checks the HTTP status and SSE framing forwards it as a normal chunk.

Failover works when an account fails before any output is sent, but not once a reply has started.

## Setup

- Agent: Pi
- Model: `glm-5.3` via the Z.ai provider, reasoning level `low`
- Routing: a group with three Z.ai accounts (one was already resting because of a 429 insufficient-balance error)
- Context size at the time: about 78k / 1.0M

## First occurrence: 502, then a mid-stream break

Sequence:

1. Pi sends a request for `glm-5.3` through the magpie gateway.
2. Account `e68d…utRM` returns 502 before any output. magpie rests it for 1 minute and forwards the request to `5f32…pQvJ`. This part works as intended.
3. Account `5f32…pQvJ` starts answering, then the upstream connection breaks.
4. Pi shows `Error: Error reading response: malformed server-sent event JSON.` and hangs. It does not retry and does not return to the prompt.

Gateway log (Routing view):

```
42d8…49iZ is resting (429 · insufficient balance, back in 19 min), placed last.
e68d…utRM (glm-5.3) at low reasoning returned 502 · failed. It rests 1 min, longer if it fails again; the request was forwarded to 5f32…pQvJ before the reply reached Pi.
Original: Post "https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4/chat/completions": read tcp [REDACTED]:51313->[REDACTED]:443: read: connection reset by peer
5f32…pQvJ (glm-5.3) at low reasoning broke after starting to answer · failed. Pi received the content already output before the error; it rests 1 min, longer if it fails again; Pi's next request goes to the other members first.
```

Upstream payload for that request:

```json
{
  "id": "202610220001118dfb145dcf634908",
  "model": "glm-5.3",
  "choices": [
    {
      "type": "message",
      "reasoning": "Attempt3 got past CF (422) but wrong ToS field name. Try common names: \"tos_accepted\", \"agreed_to_terms\", \"accept_terms\", \"terms\": true, \"acceptTos\". One more round quickly"
    }
  ],
  "error": {
    "message": "Z.ai: connection lost mid-reply (http2: client connection lost)",
    "type": "api_error"
  }
}
```

## Second occurrence: the error is embedded in the response body

The same failure happened again. The body below does not look like an error response: the partial reply is in `choices[0]`, and the failure appears only in a top-level `error` object after it.

```json
{
  "id": "202610231354108430f15556a64a7f",
  "model": "glm-5.3",
  "choices": [
    {
      "type": "message",
      "reasoning": "Now design the overhaul. Approach:\n\n1. Full rewrite of `src/ui/style.css` with a modern design system, keeping all selectors used.\n... (middle of the reply omitted; it is long and unrelated to this bug) ...\nUpdate main.ts marks: replace with SVG strings. The `mark` field renders inside span.nav-mark. I'll swap glyph chars for inline SVGs"
    }
  ],
  "error": {
    "message": "Z.ai: connection lost mid-reply (read tcp [REDACTED]:53575->[REDACTED]:443: read: connection reset by peer)",
    "type": "api_error"
  }
}
```

The reply is cut off in the middle of a sentence, and the only sign of failure is the `error` object at the end.

## Analysis

- The upstream failure itself (Z.ai returning 502 / resetting the connection) is outside magpie's control.
- Failover works when the upstream fails **before** any output (the e68d → 5f32 hop in the first log).
- When the upstream fails **after** output has started, magpie cannot switch accounts. It forwards the partial output to the agent, and the agent receives either:
  - a truncated or unparsable SSE event (`malformed server-sent event JSON`, then a hang), or
  - a chunk that looks normal but carries a top-level `error` object, which the agent may not recognize as a failure, so a half-written reply can look like a finished one.
- Z.ai does not always signal this failure through an HTTP error status or a broken stream. It can put an `error` object (`type: "api_error"`) inside the body after partial content, in a shape that is not a standard Chat Completions error (`choices[].reasoning` and a top-level `error` in the same body).

So the problem looks like error detection and stream termination after a mid-stream failure, not the failover logic itself.

## Expected behavior

1. Treat any chunk that contains a top-level `error` object (with `type: "api_error"`) as an upstream failure, even when the HTTP status was 200.
2. If nothing has been sent to the agent yet, fail over to the next member of the routing group, the same as for 502.
3. Otherwise, end the stream with a well-formed error event for the protocol the agent is using, then close the connection. For Chat Completions that means a valid error chunk followed by `data: [DONE]`. The agent should then report a failed reply and be able to retry and return to the prompt, instead of hanging or treating the partial text as a complete answer.
4. Never write a truncated SSE event to the agent.

## Actual behavior

- The agent hangs after `malformed server-sent event JSON` (first occurrence), or receives a partial reply whose failure is only visible in an embedded `error` object (second occurrence).
- The only way out is to interrupt the agent manually and resend.

## Workaround

Interrupt the agent (Ctrl+C) and resend. magpie rests the failed account for 1 minute, so the next request usually goes to another member.

issue.title: gateway: a plugin's in-stream error frame is relayed as data — its code/status never reach routing

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

A provider plugin that returns an OpenAI-compatible stream can end it with an error frame:

```
data: {"error":{"message":"...","type":"upstream_error","code":"upstream_timeout","status":504}}
```

Once the plugin has already sent `200`, that frame is **the only signal it can give** — the HTTP status is spent. Today magpie relays it as ordinary bytes: the account is not rested, the turn is not recorded as failed, and nothing downstream can tell "the model answered" from "the model died halfway".

This is not #3197 / #3346 (the upstream connection died). Here the plugin **deliberately** ended the stream and said why; the information exists and is dropped.

## Where this already works

`internal/gateway/chat.go:1311` — on the **translation** path a Chat reply's `{"error": ...}` is parsed, `filterRefused` pulls out `code` / `status`, and it becomes `Event{Kind: KError, Code, Status}`.

## Where it doesn't

`internal/gateway/gateway.go:3965` — when the provider speaks the client's own protocol (`relay == true`), the reply goes through `s.passthrough(...)`, which tidies and relays bytes. Nothing parses `{"error": ...}` on that path.

Plugin-served models always take it: a plugin's `loader.fetch` returns an OpenAI-compatible `Response`, so client and provider protocol match by construction. For **every** plugin, an in-stream error frame is opaque.

## Two concrete gaps

1. **passthrough ignores the error frame.** No `markUnfit` / rest, no failed-turn accounting — the same account keeps being picked for the same request, and the routing view shows a healthy turn.
2. **`streamFailure()` and `filterRefused()` disagree on the shape.** `internal/gateway/gateway.go:5222` writes `{"error":{"message":...,"type":"api_error"}}` with no `code` / `status`, while the Chat parser at `chat.go:1312` reads exactly those fields. So even magpie's own mid-stream failure frame carries none of the routing signal a plugin frame does.

## Questions

1. Should `passthrough` parse `{"error": ...}` at least to (a) end the stream with the protocol's own terminator and (b) record the failure / rest the account? I understand from #3197 that failover itself is impossible once output has started — I'm not asking for that.
2. Should `streamFailure()` carry `code` / `status` so a client sees the same shape whether the failure came from the plugin or from magpie?
3. If plugin-side codes are meant to be client-only, that belongs in the plugin docs (`HOOKS.md` §7 in the scaffold) — right now the scaffold tells plugin authors to set `status` on the frame, which implies the gateway reads it.

## Repro

Any plugin that ends a stream with an error frame — e.g. a provider whose runtime has a hard per-turn wall clock: the plugin watches the clock, aborts at 285s, and emits `{"error": {..., "code": "upstream_timeout", "status": 504}}`. The client gets a readable message; routing sees nothing.

## Not asking

* Changing the "once output started, no failover" rule — that's a deliberate design and #3197 settles the stream-ending part.
* Anything about pre-first-byte failover, which already works.

issue.title: gateway: a network drop mid-stream on a plugin provider hangs forever — no timeout, no retry, no error

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

A network drop in the middle of a streamed model reply leaves Magpie waiting forever when the provider is served by a plugin. There is no idle timeout, no error frame, and no retry: the request stays open until the client cancels it.

## Environment

- Magpie 0.1.1623 (macOS app, Go 1.26.8)
- Provider: `workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (plugin provider via `@magpie-community/opencode-workbuddy-auth` 0.2.13)
- Local HTTP proxy: FlClash at `127.0.0.1:7890`. When the network was cut, the proxy process stayed up and its local socket remained ESTABLISHED while its outbound path was dead.

## What happened

1. A streaming chat request was in progress. The first reasoning chunk arrived after 1.7 s (`ttft_ms = 1739`).
2. I disconnected the network for a few seconds and restored it. The upstream stream never resumed.
3. Magpie kept the request open for 4 min 52 s (`292593 ms`) with no further bytes, no error, and no retry. The client (Grok Build) eventually canceled it (`status 499`, `error_message: "the agent canceled the request"`).
4. The usage row for route `1793086980553` records `input_tokens=0`, `output_tokens=0`, and no retry.
5. In the client log: `shell.turn.inference_start` at 20:54:49, no `inference_done` until cancellation at 20:59:42.

## Why it hangs

The plugin path bypasses the gateway's normal upstream transport:

- `internal/provider/plugins.go`: `Provider.Do` calls `p.Account.transport(req)` first, which for a plugin provider is `pluginFetch`. The request never goes through `http.Client` / `upstreamTransport`, so `upstreamHeaderWait` (`ResponseHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Minute`) and `netproxy.HTTP2Health()` do not apply.
- `internal/plugin/host.go`: `Fetch` waits on the plugin's reply head/body with no deadline; `body.Read` only returns on queued chunks, context cancellation, body close, or host death (`TestHostBodyCancelEndsAStalledRead` covers only the cancel path).
- `internal/plugin/host.js`: `fetchAs` calls Bun's `fetch` with only `signal: ctl.signal`. There is no `AbortSignal.timeout` and no per-chunk idle timer. When the local proxy socket stays open but no data arrives, `for await (const chunk of res.body)` blocks forever.
- `internal/gateway/gateway.go`: the relay loop `n, err := rd.Read(buf)` has no read deadline. `cutMidReply()` only runs when `rd.Read` returns an error; a silent socket never returns one, so the client receives no `connection lost mid-reply` event.
- Retries happen only before any content is sent. Once the first token is forwarded there is no failover; the plugin fetch only retries a 401, not network failures.

This differs from #2529 / #2843 / #3197: those concern built-in providers (10-minute response-header timeout / HTTP/2 silent connection). Here the plugin provider has no response-header timeout at all, and the stream is already past the first chunk.

## Expected behavior

- A stalled plugin fetch should end after an idle timeout (e.g. no body bytes for 30–120 s): abort the plugin fetch and close the stream with a protocol-valid error event, so the agent can retry or show an error.
- Optionally retry on a fresh connection when nothing has been sent yet; when content has already been forwarded, end the stream with the error.
- Make the timeout configurable per provider/model if possible (similar to the request in #2529).

## Workaround

Cancel the running turn and resend; that is what recovered this session. Restarting Magpie would also clear it, but is heavy-handed.

### 2. 48,000 是上游硬边界，但没人告诉 magpie

| 插件模型列表（`plugin-providers.json`） | **`output: 0`（未知）** |
| **Qoder 服务端实际** | **48000** |

插件侧 `configModel()` / `runtimeModel()` 把 `limit.output` 硬写成 `0`（`index.mjs` 中的 `limit: { context: m.context ?? 0, output: 0 }`，两处），因为 Qoder 的 model list 响应里根本没有 output 上限字段。于是 magpie 只能拿 128000 这个更大的值，一路发到上游被无声截断。

### 3. dsh 侧看到的与真实情况不符

dsh 的 `max_tokens` 取自 `modelOutputs` 的 128000，请求发出后上游按 48000 截断。dsh 收到 `finish_reason: "length"` → `turn/end {kind:"max-tokens"}` → 渲染「已达到输出 token 上限，发送"继续"可让模型接着输出」。**这个提示在本次是错的**：不是回复写不完，是模型把全部预算烧在了推理上、一个字都没输出。

## 我认为可以改的地方

按重要度排序，前两条是我真正想提的：

1. **「推理吃满预算、正文为空」这条路径现在完全没有出口。** 两道闸门都放它过去，而且这次是叠加的：

   - `emptyFails(actual)` 只对 `CodeAssist` 和 `Gemini` 返回 true，Chat 上游（qoder 走的就是 Chat）**根本不进**空回复检查；
   - 即便进了，`answersNothing("length")` 也会返回 false——注释写明 `length` 就是「all reasoning」那种情形。

   两者合起来的结果是：一个 `stop=length` 且 `saidAnything(parts)==false`（只有 Thinking 块，无 text、无 tool call）的回复，被当作正常的 200 交给客户端。建议在 Chat 侧补一个出口：`stop == "length"` 且 `!saidAnything` 时，走 `emptyReply` 那条路（或至少带上明确的错误/警告），让 dsh 这类 agent 拿到可重试的错误，而不是一个误导性的「继续」。

2. **插件应报出真实的 output 上限（或 magpie 不应把「未知」当「无上限」）。** 上游 `output: 0` 现在被当成「没有声明」，magpie 落回 128000，与真实的 48000 差 2.67 倍。哪怕拿不到精确值，把 qoder 这类「未知」保守成一个已知安全值（如 32000，插件自己的 `qoderBody` 默认就是 32000）也比发 128000 更诚实。

3. （次要，供参考）`usage.jsonl` 里 qoder 插件请求的 `session` / `native_session` 字段为空，导致没法直接按会话聚合，只能按时间窗对齐。如果方便的话补上会好查很多。

## 环境

- magpie `0.1.1292`，macOS，arm64
- 插件 `@magpie-community/opencode-qoder-auth@0.2.19`（moved：`migrations.json` 里 `qoder.state == "plugin"`）
- provider `qoder`，模型 `dfmodel`；`reasoningEfforts` 有 low / high / max，其中 4 次截断里 3 次是 `effort=max`
- 客户端 DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2，profile `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop`，provider `magpie`（`openai-completions`，`http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1`）
- 该 provider 是 moved 订阅，所以按 `AGENTS.md` 的划分，第 2 条的修复应落在 `magpie-community/plugins` 的 `packages/qoder`，再抬 `internal/provider/migrate_qoder.go` 的 `min`（当前 `0.2.11`）；第 1 条在 magpie 本仓库。

---

补充一句给审核者的判断依据：这次真正的问题不在「上限是多少」，而在**一个 reasoning 用满 100% 预算、正文为空的回复被当作成功回复交回客户端**。上限调成 48000 只是让截断来得更早，agent 仍然会收到一个「继续」的假信号。

issue.title: gateway (Chat relay): an upstream reply that ends without a finish_reason is relayed verbatim, and strict OpenAI clients (pi-ai / DSH) throw the whole turn away with "Stream ended without finish_reason"

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

When magpie **relays** a Chat upstream's stream (the client speaks Chat and the provider serves the model on Chat — e.g. `minimax-cn/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`), and the upstream's stream ends **without a `finish_reason` chunk** (and without `data: [DONE]`), magpie relays the bytes exactly as they came and closes the connection. The client therefore gets a stream that has content but no terminal frame.

A strict OpenAI reader (pi-ai — the library DeepSeek Harness embeds) requires a `finish_reason` and throws:

```
Stream ended without finish_reason
```

classified as a transport error, so the agent retries the whole request (up to 5×) and then loses the turn. magpie records the call as a plain `200` with **no error**, so **nothing appears in app.log either** — the failure is invisible on both sides.

## The stream the client actually receives

Captured from the running gateway (2026-11-05, `http://127.0.0.1:15113/v1/chat/completions`, model `minimax-cn/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`):

```
data: {"id":"073a…","choices":[{"delta":{"role":"assistant"}}],"created":…,"model":"minimax-cn/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash","object":"chat.completion.chunk","usage":null}
data: {"id":"073a…","choices":[{"delta":{"role":"assistant","reasoning_content":"…"}}],…}
data: {"id":"073a…","choices":[{"delta":{"tool_calls":[{"index":0,"id":"call_…","type":"function","function":{"name":"bash","arguments":""}}]}}],…}
data: {"id":"073a…","choices":[{"delta":{"tool_calls":[{"function":{"arguments":"…"}}]}}],…}
<connection closed — no finish_reason chunk, no data: [DONE]>
```

The tool call itself is complete and well-formed (its `arguments` parse as valid JSON); only the terminal frame is missing.

## Why the client throws

pi-ai's openai-completions reader (vendored in DSH's `app.asar`):

```js
const choice = Array.isArray(chunk.choices) ? chunk.choices[0] : undefined;
if (!choice) continue;
if (choice.finish_reason) { …; hasFinishReason = true; }
…
if ((compat.supportsFinishReason && !hasFinishReason) || output.stopReason === "pending")
    throw new Error("Stream ended without finish_reason");
```

No `finish_reason` ⇒ the turn is thrown away. Two related notes: pi-ai has **no `chunk.error` branch**, so an `{"error":…}` chunk (the other shape this bug takes) is dropped silently as well; and DSH's provider entry carries no `compat`, so `supportsFinishReason` defaults to `true` and there is no client-side tolerance to fall back on.

## Where magpie stands today (source)

The reply is **relayed**, not translated — `internal/gateway/gateway.go`:

```go
relayable := slices.Contains(s.usable(p, model), from) && (p.Account == nil || !p.Account.Stream || streamOf(body) || gathers(p, from, body))
```

`usable(minimax-cn, model)` is `[Chat, Anthropic]` (Chat first — `MessagesFirst` is only for Claude models), so a Chat client gets the upstream's Chat stream relayed byte for byte. The relayed chunks even carry MiniMax's own `base_resp` field, which magpie's own encoder never writes — so these are the upstream's bytes, verbatim.

In the relay path, a lost `finish_reason` **is** filled in — but only behind a gate:

```go
// a Chat stream of Gemini's OpenAI-compatible API is whole only with
// its finish_reason, [DONE] or not (saysItsEnd)
unfinished := proto == provider.Chat && sniff.failed == "" && sniff.u.Stop == "" && saysItsEnd(p, proto, upstream)
if fin := sniff.tail.finish(); sse && unfinished && fin != "" && (rerr == nil || rerr == io.EOF) && r.Context().Err() == nil {
    // only the finish_reason was lost, after the generation was done
    // (chatTail): the client gets it, and the reply is whole.
    dropHalf()
    w.Write(append(apart(), "data: "+string(finishChunk(fin))+"\n\n"...))
    if !sniff.ended {
        w.Write([]byte("data: [DONE]\n\n"))
    }
    …
}
```

`saysItsEnd` (`internal/gateway/continuation.go`):

```go
func saysItsEnd(p provider.Provider, proto provider.Protocol, model string) bool {
    switch {
    case proto == provider.Anthropic, proto == provider.Responses, geminiKin(proto):
        return true
    case proto == provider.Chat:
        return geminiCompat(p.Host(), model) || p.Host() == commandCodeHost
    }
    return false
}
```

For a Chat upstream it is true only for **Gemini's OpenAI-compatible API** and **Command Code**. For `minimax-cn` it is false ⇒ no fill-in, no `[DONE]`, and the reply is relayed as it came.

The project's own docs describe the class of problem and the client-side asymmetry (`docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md`):

> a Chat stream may end without `[DONE]` and be whole

which is true for a lenient reader and not for a strict one. The same file already records the strict-client case — for Gemini's API only:

> Linka on Discord: the upstream hung up between a whole function call and its `finish_reason`, and Pi threw the call away as "Stream ended without finish_reason"

i.e. the fill-in was added because of exactly this client behaviour; the other Chat upstreams were not covered.

## Observed impact

- **64 occurrences** in one DeepSeek Harness session on 2026-11-04 (≈5 % of ~1270 model calls), each retried 5× by the client before the turn was lost.
- The failing calls are **not** in magpie's `app.log`: the call is recorded as `status 200` with an empty error, and `failedCallLine` skips a 200 with no error.
- They cluster in the largest sessions (≈360 k–440 k prompt tokens, 48 tool definitions); sessions on the same provider with a small context had **zero** occurrences — so the upstream ending without a `finish_reason` appears to depend on the size of the request rather than being constant.

## Suggested fix

1. **Widen the `chatTail` fill-in** from `geminiCompat` to any Chat upstream whose stream ended without a `finish_reason`. The code above already does the right thing; only the gate needs widening (e.g. `saysItsEnd` answering "yes" for a Chat upstream that actually ended without a `finish_reason`, or a separate check keyed on `sniff.u.Stop == ""`).
2. **When even the usage is missing** (`sniff.tail.finish() == ""`, so there is nothing to fill in), still append `data: [DONE]` so a strict reader stops at a well-formed boundary instead of reading to a closed connection. The severed case already does this — `if proto == provider.Chat && rerr != nil && rerr != io.EOF { w.Write([]byte("data: [DONE]\n\n")) }` (#3197) — the *clean end* case has no counterpart.
3. **Record it in the usage/routing record** with a stop that says what happened (e.g. `stop: ""` → `stop: "ended_short"`), so the Routing page and `app.log` show it instead of a clean 200.

## Client-side workaround meanwhile

For a strict reader that must live with this, `compat.supportsFinishReason: false` on the provider entry makes the missing `finish_reason` be read as `toolUse`/`stop` instead of an error (the tool call in these cases is complete, so the turn can proceed). That hides the real cause, though — the fill-in above is the proper fix.

## How to capture a real occurrence

The upstream ending without a `finish_reason` is intermittent and, in our runs, only seen with a very large prompt. Either:

- turn on the local request archive (Settings › …) and replay a failing request, or
- read the relay's own bytes and look for a stream that ends with neither a `finish_reason` chunk nor `data: [DONE]`:

```bash
curl -N http://127.0.0.1:15113/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer magpie' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"minimax-cn/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say OK"}],"tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"bash","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"command":{"type":"string"}}}}]}'
```

## Environment

- magpie **0.1.2909** (during the session) / **0.1.3002** (today), macOS darwin/arm64
- provider `minimax-cn` (MiniMax China, `https://api.minimaxi.com/v1`), model `minimax-cn/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`
- client: DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.5**, provider `magpie` (`openai-completions`, `http://127.0.0.1:15113/v1`), `reasoning_effort: max`, 48 tools, ≈360 k–440 k prompt tokens

## Related

- #3197 — mid-stream upstream failure in the relay path leaves Pi with malformed SSE (its `[DONE]` fix covers a *failed read*; this is the *clean end* case)
- #2533 — a stream that began and then failed is handed to Pi as `api_error` (the error-event shape of the same family)
- #2471 — a 200 stream that ends with `finish_reason:"error"` is counted as a success
- #1562 — a translated Responses reply cut by the upstream ends with an error instead of a whole delivery

issue.body:
## Description
When using magpie with pi agent against Z.ai (model `glm-5.3`) with multi-account rotation, 
a mid-stream upstream disconnect causes pi agent to crash with:

    Error: Error reading response: malformed server-sent event JSON.

## Environment
- magpie version / commit: <fill in>
- pi agent version: <fill in>
- OS: <fill in>
- Upstream: Z.ai, model `glm-5.3`
- Multi-account rotation: enabled (<N> accounts)
- Proxy/VPN in use: <yes/no>

## What happened
The upstream connection was reset while the model was still streaming its reasoning. 
The client received this payload (instead of a well-formed SSE event / proper stream termination):

    {
      "id": "2026101620...",
      "model": "glm-5.3",
      "choices": [
        {
          "type": "message",
          "reasoning": "...(truncated mid-sentence) ... the VM program itself hit an undefined"
        }
      ],
      "error": {
        "message": "Z.ai: connection lost mid-reply (read tcp [<redacted>]:57307->[<redacted>]:443: read: connection reset by peer)",
        "type": "api_error"
      }
    }

pi agent's SSE parser then fails with "malformed server-sent event JSON".

## Expected behavior
Any of the following would be better:
1. If the failure happens before/early in the stream, retry with the same or next account in the rotation.
2. If it happens mid-stream, emit a properly formatted SSE error event (`data: {...}\n\n`, then `data: [DONE]` or close cleanly) so clients can handle it, rather than a bare/truncated JSON.
3. Mark the affected account as temporarily unhealthy so rotation can skip it.

## Steps to reproduce
Intermittent. Happens with long reasoning outputs on glm-5.3 via rotated Z.ai accounts.
1. Configure magpie with multiple Z.ai accounts
2. Run pi agent with `glm-5.3` on a long-running task
3. Occasionally the upstream resets the connection mid-reply

## Logs
<attach magpie logs around the timestamp, redacted>

## Additional notes
Upstream IPs were IPv6; not sure if IPv6 routing is a factor. 
Happy to test a fix or provide more logs.

The boundary you flagged is real — confirmed from the source, and fixed on a fork branch.

An `event:` name line goes out as soon as it completes. An upstream that dies between the name and its `data:` line therefore leaves the client an event block with a name and no data, closed by the blank line the relay's ending writes. Upstream's own severed-stream test for this shape (`TestPassthroughStreamEndsOnLineEnd`, Messages) constructs exactly the cut and asserts only that the error event begins after a blank line — the empty event before it goes unchallenged. Chat was spared because its SSE has no `event:` lines, which is why the fix this issue landed upstream (`70a40aaa0`, the `[DONE]` ending) never hit this: the orphan needs a named-events route (Responses, Messages, Gemini).

Fix on [`fix/3197-orphan-event`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3197-orphan-event) (head `a5fa3228f996808dc8c2d1628fb89103bafadee4`, on `upstream/main` `c736906b1`): a named event whose data has not come is held back and goes out when the data line does; a name the upstream itself never follows with data is relayed as the upstream sent it (the ended-short path, unchanged); on a sever the held name drops with the half line, so the client's stream ends with whole events only, then the error.

Tests, red on clean `upstream/main` and green at the head: `TestPassthroughResponsesSeveredAfterEventName` (cut right after a name) and `TestPassthroughResponsesSeveredMidData` (cut inside the data line), each asserting no event block without data and the failure named; the whole severed family (`TestPassthroughStreamCutMidLine`, `EndsOnLineEnd`, the Chat severed cases, `TestLoopCutMidLine`) stays green. Full gateway run attached in evidence.

Not verified against a live Codex + openai SDK 7.19.0 client — the SDK's behavior on an empty-data event is taken from your report, and the wire shape before the fix matches what you predicted from the source.

@skygunner's fix is verified on today's main (`7dbfc9f2f`): cherry-picked onto it cleanly (branch [hunt-20261112-t1-3197](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/hunt-20261112-t1-3197), head `abe40fd1486611f6`, tree identical under `git am` of the patch below), and it does what the follow-up needs: an `event:` name whose data has not come is held back until the data line does, so a severed stream ends the client's read with whole events only, then the relay's error event.

**Red without the fix** (their two tests, the product hunk in gateway.go reverted, tests kept): `TestPassthroughResponsesSeveredAfterEventName` and `TestPassthroughResponsesSeveredMidData` both fail on the unpatched gateway — the name-only event block goes out, closed by the ending's blank line, exactly the shape DDDFXYqiming's client parsed as "malformed server-sent event JSON".

**Green with the fix**: the two tests, the whole severed family around them (`TestPassthroughStreamCutMidLine`, `TestPassthroughStreamEndsOnLineEnd`, the Chat severed cases, `TestLoopCut*`), and the full `./internal/gateway` package — ok, 997 s, zero failures. gofmt and go vet clean.

**Boundary kept as posted**: a name the upstream itself never follows with data (a stream that ends short on its own, not severed) still relays as it came — the hold-back is on the severed path only, which is the path the client-side parse error came from.

**Not verified**: a live Codex + openai Node SDK 7.19.0 client (the SDK's empty-data behavior is taken from DDDFXYqiming's report, as in skygunner's post).
